text: Then King David said to the whole assembly: "My son Solomon, the one whom God has chosen, is young and inexperienced, and the work is great; for this palace is not for man but for the LORD God.

With all my strength I have made provision for the house of my God: gold for the gold work, silver for the silver, bronze for the bronze, iron for the iron, and wood for the wood; also onyx stones and stones for settings, stones of antimony and of many colors, every kind of precious stone, and marble in abundance.
Moreover, because of my delight in the house of my God, I now give for the house of my God my own treasure of gold and silver, over and above all that I have provided for the holy house:
three thousand talents of gold, gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, for overlaying the walls of the buildings,
gold for the gold work and silver for the silver, and for all the work to be done by the craftsmen. Now who will offer himself willingly, consecrating himself today to the LORD?"
Then the leaders of the families, the officers of the tribes of Israel, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials in charge of the king's work gave willingly.

For the service of the house of God they gave five thousand talents and ten thousand darics of gold, ten thousand talents of silver, eighteen thousand talents of bronze, and a hundred thousand talents of iron.
Whoever had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the house of the LORD, into the care of Jehiel the Gershonite.
The people rejoiced at their willing response, for they had given freely and wholeheartedly to the LORD. King David also rejoiced greatly.
Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of the whole assembly, saying: "Blessed are you, LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.

Yours, LORD, is the greatness and the power and the glory and the victory and the majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is yours. Yours, LORD, is the kingdom, and you are exalted as head over all.
Riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all. In your hand are strength and might, and it is in your power to make great and to give strength to all.
And now, our God, we give you thanks and praise your glorious name.
But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give so willingly as this? For everything comes from you, and from your hand we have given to you.
We are strangers before you, and sojourners, as all our fathers were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, and there is no hope of remaining.
LORD our God, all this abundance that we have provided for building you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and all of it is yours.

I know, my God, that you test the heart and delight in what is right. With an upright heart I have freely offered all these things, and now I have seen with joy how your people who are here have given willingly to you.
LORD, God of our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, keep this desire in the hearts of your people forever, and direct their hearts to you.
And give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, to carry out everything, and to build the palace for which I have made provision."

Then David said to the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God!" And the whole assembly praised the LORD, the God of their fathers, and they bowed their heads and prostrated themselves before the LORD and before the king.

versions.text: Then David said to the whole assembly, "Praise the LORD your God!" And the whole assembly praised the LORD, the God of their fathers, and they bowed low and knelt before the LORD and before the king.
versions.explanation: The two Hebrew verbs describe bowing the head (qadad) and then full prostration (hishtachavah). "Knelt" weakens the second verb and reverses the natural intensification; "bowed their heads and prostrated themselves" is more accurate and reads well aloud.

text: The next day they sacrificed to the LORD and offered burnt offerings to him: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs, with their drink offerings, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. Then they made Solomon son of David king a second time; they anointed him before the LORD as ruler, and Zadok as priest.
So Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king in place of his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him.
All the officials and the mighty men, and all the sons of King David as well, pledged their allegiance to King Solomon.
The LORD exalted Solomon greatly in the sight of all Israel and bestowed on him such royal majesty as no king over Israel had ever had before him.
David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel.
He reigned over Israel forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem.
He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor, and his son Solomon reigned in his place.
The acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet, and the records of Gad the seer,
together with all the details of his reign and his power, and the events that came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the other lands.

versions.text: together with all the details of his reign and his power, and the events that came upon him and upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the surrounding lands.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads simply "all the kingdoms of the lands"; "surrounding" adds a nuance not present in the text.
